  "title": "Keyserver Sync Preference per Key",
  "body": "To bundle discussion about keyserver sync issues, I opened this issue.\nThis is basically copy paste from: https://github.com/open-keychain/open-keychain/wiki/Google-Summer-of-Code-2016#keyserver-sync-preference-per-key\n\nSo our current idea how to handle this is as follows, feedback welcome:\nWhile communication with keyservers and upload of keys is a feature of OpenKeychain which technically works, this area is quite lacking in usability. Many users have also expressed a desire to keep their keys off keyservers. A good way to deal with both of these problems is to mark the user's keys on creation whether they should be distributed via keyservers or not, and equivalently making other keys aware of whether they are already available on keyservers or have been obtained by different means. This information should then be used as a basis to decide how to deal with publication of certificates, and solve cases where a key has new certifictes locally but is not updated on keyservers.\n\nExpected results: A per-key preference on whether the key should be kept in sync with keyservers, and relevant behavior based on that preference.\n",

      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "I just signed up to GitHub to tell you developers how mad I am that your little app just uploaded my public key and e-mail-address to a keyserver without asking for permission. Oh wait, I should have first started the app without internet connection to uncheck the \"Synchronize with the internet\" checkbox, which is checked by default, so that it has no chance to upload the keys before I even have a clue what is happening? Is that how people have to use the app that don't want to get spammed to death? Are you serious? \r\n\r\nMy e-mail address, which I have used for over a decade and which I only use for private communication, will probably soon be spammed to death. Thank you very much! \r\nPlease tell me, when one develops such an app, how can one be so ignorant of user privacy? Is it because you have ideas like the following in your head?\r\n> Keeping public key material secret makes no sense.\r\n\r\nIf you have so smart ideas, please develop an app that can remove my e-mail-address from the servers again."

      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "Hi there, \r\nI also have a rather big problem with uploading keys to keyservers, and would like to bring up something else. do I get it correctly that right now confirming a key also automatically means uploading it? \r\n\r\nI have imported a few keys of other people in my keychain, mostly directly from emails those people sent me, with attached public keys. I know that I can trust those keys, since I verified them by talking to those people personally. Can I somehow mark those keys as \"trusted\", without signing them, and without uploading them to a keyserver? I did not try what acually happens I \"confirm\" other peoples keys, but as far as I understood the dialog, it will sign and upload the public key of my contacts. Is this true?\r\n\r\nAutomatically uploading own keys is one thing that should not happen. But uploading keys of **others** to a keyserver without them knowing, is completely unacceptable in my opinion.  At the very least, make this opt-in. And as fast as possible, before many people publish their entire address book on public keyservers where all the spammers and scammers can get them. I never wrote code for apps before, but removing the default-tick on all the checkboxes that synchronize with keyservers should be an easy patch before this discussion reached a better conclusion. \r\n\r\nCould someone do this?   \r\n\r\n"
    }
